@graph.headline: The Exit Cost of Rented AI: What Cloud Dependency Actually Costs a Metro Detroit Business Over Three Years
@graph.description: Cloud AI looks cheap because you only ever see one line of the bill. Here is the three-year math for a ten-person Metro Detroit practice, the two costs the invoice hides, and the honest volume threshold where renting still wins.

about.name: The total cost of ownership of cloud AI versus on-premises local LLM deployment, including break-even thresholds by token volume, hidden cloud costs, data breach and shadow AI exposure, and the seven layers of AI vendor lock-in

keywords: local LLM total cost of ownership

mainEntity.name: How much does cloud AI actually cost a small business?

acceptedAnswer.text: At two million tokens a day, a ten-person practice spends roughly $2,600 a year on inference at mid-tier API pricing — about $7,938 over three years, before retry overhead and integration labor.

mainEntity.name: When does an on-premises LLM pay for itself?

acceptedAnswer.text: It is a volume threshold, not a duration. Against a $3,499 device with about $26 a month in electricity, payback runs about 18 months at two million tokens a day and seven months at five million. Below one million a day it typically never pays back on cost alone.

mainEntity.name: What are the hidden costs of cloud AI that the invoice doesn't show?

acceptedAnswer.text: Retry overhead (about $1,800 a year per percentage point at a $180,000 base spend), rate-limit engineering, 5 to 15% payload bloat, and vendor-side pricing and model-deprecation changes you do not control.

mainEntity.name: What does it actually cost to switch AI vendors?

acceptedAnswer.text: More than the price difference. Lock-in lives in seven layers — model API, prompt library, evaluation harness, fine-tunes, caching strategy, observability, and billing — and prompts, evals, and fine-tunes are tied to one model's behavior, so a switch is a re-validation project rather than a provider change.

mainEntity.name: Is it cheaper to run AI locally or use an API?

acceptedAnswer.text: It depends on volume and on what your data is worth. Below roughly one million tokens a day the API is cheaper, often decisively; above five million the owned side is several times cheaper. In between, breach exposure, privilege, and switching cost decide it.

mainEntity.name: Is shadow AI a real risk for a small practice, or just a large-enterprise problem?

acceptedAnswer.text: It is worse for small practices, because they rarely have detection. Endpoint telemetry across 420,000+ corporate devices found 58.4% of employees using unsanctioned AI tools and 24.1% pasting sensitive corporate data into an external prompt, while only 38.4% of organizations could detect it.
